title: quantization-nan-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-04
content:
Summary / goal:
- Track debugging notes for intermittent NaNs and quality regressions observed after enabling INT8/FP8 quantization profiles on the 7B/13B family.
- Primary symptom: occasional NaN logits and 'loss: nan' during short evals; more frequent when using fp8-mantissa optimized kernels and per-tensor scales on some layers.

Repro notes (high level):
- Model: rwd-7b-v1 (transformer, RMSNorm + rotary).
- Baselines: FP32 and BF16 run cleanly.
- Quant modes tried: INT8 per-channel (weights only), INT8 per-tensor, FP8 E4M3, BF16 activation-only.
- Failures primarily when enabling activation quantization + FP8 kernels.

Commands I ran:
- python tools/quantize.py --model checkpoints/rwd-7b-v1 --out quant/rwd-7b-int8-pc --bits 8 --scheme per_channel --calib-dataset data/calib_small.json
- python run_eval.py --model quant/rwd-7b-int8-pc --dtype int8 --batch 4 --prompt-file eval/prompts.txt --dump-activations activations/int8-pc/
- python run_eval.py --model quant/rwd-7b-fp8-e4m3 --dtype fp8 --batch 1 --prompt-file eval/prompts.txt --trace-level debug
- (internal) ri-run --model rwd-7b-v1 --quant=fp8 --kernel=fast-fp8 --trace /tmp/trace.log

Observed error snippets / traces:
- eval run (int8 activation + per-tensor) stdout:
  Step 12/50 loss: 8.271
  Step 13/50 loss: nan
  RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in exp (softmax)
  RuntimeError: NaN encountered in attention_scores at layer 8

- trace.log (fp8 run):
  [2026-03-03T14:22:10Z] layer12: att_scores max=1.2e+38 min=-1.1e+38 -> after softmax produced inf/nan
  [2026-03-03T14:22:10Z] kernel fast-fp8: scale_factor=2.3e-2, clip_threshold=127
  [2026-03-03T14:22:10Z] fallback to fp16 path not available (dedicated kernel mismatch)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization scales are too coarse for some attention layers -> softmax exponent overflows -> NaN. Per-tensor scale for activations causes dynamic range loss; per-channel reduced but not eliminated.
2) Loss of precision in RMSNorm / layernorm (small denominators) when using fp8 -> division leads to inf -> propagated NaN.
3) Kernel bug in fast-fp8 path: incorrect clamp/round order or missing denorm handling.
4) Calibration dataset not representative -> out-of-distribution activation ranges at inference time.
5) KV cache accumulation with quantized activations leads to progressive growth due to rounding bias.

Quick checks I ran (results):
- Re-run with BF16 activations: problem disappeared in short evals -> suggests precision / dynamic range issue.
- INT8 per-channel weights + FP32 activations: no NaNs -> points to activation quantization being suspect.
- INT8 per-tensor activations + per-channel weights: intermittent NaNs -> per-tensor activations are risky.
- Dumped layer stats for run that produced NaN: layer 8 att_scores max ~ 1.2e+38 -> suggests overflow.
- Re-ran with smaller batch size (1) and no fp8 kernel: stable.

Debug steps / TODO (next actions):
- [ ] Add NaN/Inf sanitizer early in runtime to dump first NaN-producing tensor + layer id + pre-quantization stats. (quick patch)
- [ ] Re-run calibration using larger, high-diversity dataset (include long tails and punctuation-heavy prompts).
- [ ] Compare per-channel vs per-tensor activation ranges: script to compute histograms per-layer across calibration set (scripts/activation_stats.py).
- [ ] Add temporary clamping in softmax input (e.g., clamp logits to +/- 50) to see whether NaN disappears; if yes, it's overflow.
- [ ] Instrument RMSNorm: dump variances near zero and add epsilon increase to test stability.
- [ ] Run with denorms flushed and IEEE flags set to trap FP exceptions (gdb/UBSAN) on kernel failing run.
- [ ] Reproduce failing run under ASAN/TSAN on CPU emulation if possible (to catch misordered memory ops).
- [ ] File a runtime bug if fast-fp8 kernel shows missing denorm handling: attach trace + minimal reproducer.

Short-term mitigations applied so far:
- Disabled fast-fp8 kernel on staging: no regressions after disable (patch reverted to safer fp16 fallback).
- Enabled per-channel activation scaling for suspect layers 6-10 as a band-aid.

Notes / ideas:
- Might be worthwhile to use symmetric vs asymmetric quantization and check zero-point behavior for attention softmax inputs. Asymmetric zero-point errors can shift logits and cause one side of distribution to blow up after exp.
- Consider calibrating with outlier-aware scale (e.g., percentile 99.999) and then use dynamic activation clipping during first N tokens.
- For fp8, check exponent bias/overflow threshold used by our kernels; E4M3 vs E5M2 has different dynamic ranges. We may be using E4M3 but thought E5M2 could be safer for attention layers.

Scratch timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-03-02: First NaN observed in A/B eval after enabling FP8 in canary (staging).
- 2026-03-03: Reproduced locally with --trace, found layer 8 att_scores huge. Disabled fast-fp8 kernel, temporary fix.
- 2026-03-04: Start deeper instrumentation + plan for calibration rerun.

Attachments / where I put dumps:
- activations/int8-pc/ (layer-wise dumps from failing run)
- traces/trace-2026-03-03.log (fp8 fast kernel trace)

Useful commands for follow-up:
- python tools/activation_stats.py --input activations/int8-pc/ --out stats/int8-pc-layer-stats.json
- python -c "import numpy as np; a=np.load('activations/layer8.npy'); print(a.max(), a.min(), np.isnan(a).any())"

Questions for the team:
- Priya: do we have a recommended fp8 format for attention-heavy models? E4M3 or E5M2 in practice?
- Ethan: can infra build an image with FP exception traps enabled for one staging node?

Immediate decision: keep fast-fp8 disabled in staging and disable activation quantization by default until we have robust per-layer calibration and NaN sanitizer in place.

-- Maya
